method.description: The source was opened read-only and copied byte for byte into an image file. SHA-256 and MD5 were computed on the plaintext stream while it was read, before any other processing. The written image was re-read and re-hashed to confirm the copy. Recordings were then located by their bitstream structure, not by any index on the source, so recordings deleted from the recorder's index are recovered along with the rest.

integrity.statement: The image on disk was re-hashed after writing and matched the hash computed while reading the source, so the copy is identical to what was read. Each recovered fragment was hashed from the image before encryption; any later change to a fragment or to the image is detectable by recomputing these digests.

Recordings were recovered by generic bitstream carving, which reads the video structure itself and not the recorder's own index.

No wall-clock time is recoverable from the video bitstream alone. Any date or time in this material must come from the recorder's own index or from the operator, and the recorder's clock should be compared with a reference clock before times are relied on.
Order is the order fragments appear in the image, which is the recording order only if the recorder had not wrapped around and started overwriting.
No wall-clock time is available from a bare elementary stream; all times are relative to the start of their own channel.
